label: Has friend relation
summary: Whether the character has the friend relation with the given character.
details: It checks the game's scripted relationship "friend" between the two characters. Vanilla uses it very often, mostly with `root` or a saved scope as the other character.

label: Has grudge relation
summary: Whether the character has the grudge relation with the given character.
details: It checks the game's scripted relationship "grudge" between the two characters. Vanilla uses it rarely.

label: Has guardian relation
summary: Whether the given character is the character's guardian.
details: It checks the scripted guardian relationship between the two characters. Vanilla uses it with saved scopes such as a recipient or a guardian. The game's relation definitions pair guardian with ward, so `has_relation_ward` checks the same pair from the other side.

label: Has intrigue mentor relation
summary: Whether the given character is the character's intrigue mentor.
details: The character it runs on is then the intrigue student: the game's relation definitions pair the two. The input shows no vanilla use.

label: Has intrigue student relation
summary: Whether the given character is an intrigue student of the character.
details: The character it runs on is then the intrigue mentor: the game's relation definitions pair the two. The input shows no vanilla use.

label: Has lover relation
summary: Whether the character has the lover relation with the given character.
details: It checks the game's scripted relationship "lover" between the two characters. Vanilla uses it very often, mostly with `root` as the other character.

label: Has mentor relation
summary: Whether the given character is the character's mentor.
details: It checks the scripted relationship "mentor" between the two characters. Vanilla gives it saved scopes such as a teacher or a helpful councillor.

label: Has nemesis relation
summary: Whether the character has the nemesis relation with the given character.
details: It checks the game's scripted relationship "nemesis" between the two characters. Vanilla uses it often, mostly with `root`, a councillor or an actor.

label: Has nursed child relation
summary: Whether the given character is a nursed child of the character.
details: The character it runs on is then the wet nurse: the game's relation definitions pair nursed child with wet nurse. Vanilla uses it only twice, both times with `root`.

label: Has oaf relation
summary: Whether the character has the oaf relation with the given character.
details: It checks a scripted relationship called oaf. Vanilla uses it once, with a `$CHARACTER$` placeholder, so what it means in play is not confirmed here.

label: Has old flame relation
summary: Whether the character has the old flame relation with the given character.
details: It checks a scripted relationship called old flame. Going by its name it is a former romance, but the input does not say so. Vanilla uses it once.

label: Has potential friend relation
summary: Whether the character has the potential friend relation with the given character.
details: It checks the scripted relationship "potential friend". Going by its name it comes before a friendship, but the input does not say how it arises. Vanilla uses it often, mostly with `root`.

label: Has potential hook relation
summary: Whether the character has the potential hook relation with the given character.
details: It checks a scripted relationship called potential hook. Vanilla uses it once, with a `$CHARACTER$` placeholder, so what it means in play is not confirmed here.

label: Has potential lover relation
summary: Whether the character has the potential lover relation with the given character.
details: It checks the scripted relationship "potential lover". Going by its name it comes before a love affair, but the input does not say how it arises. Vanilla uses it with saved scopes such as `lover_1` and `lover_2`, and `root`.

label: Has potential rival relation
summary: Whether the character has the potential rival relation with the given character.
details: It checks the scripted relationship "potential rival". Going by its name it comes before a rivalry, but the input does not say how it arises. Vanilla uses it often, mostly with `root`.

label: Has rival relation
summary: Whether the character has the rival relation with the given character.
details: It checks the game's scripted relationship "rival" between the two characters. Vanilla uses it very often, mostly with `root`.

label: Has soldier friend relation
summary: Whether the character has the soldier friend relation with the given character.
details: It checks a scripted relationship called soldier friend. The input shows no vanilla use, so what creates it is not confirmed here.

label: Has soulmate relation
summary: Whether the character has the soulmate relation with the given character.
details: It checks the game's scripted relationship "soulmate" between the two characters. Vanilla uses it often, mostly with `root`.

label: Has student relation
summary: Whether the given character is a student of the character.
details: The character it runs on is then the mentor: the game's relation definitions pair student with mentor. Vanilla uses it only twice.

label: Has any relation to
summary: Whether the character has some relation to the given character.
details: The game's documentation says it matches the data function `HasRelationTo`, so it is a general check and not tied to one named relation. Vanilla uses it with saved scopes such as siege, battle, army and occupation owners and victims. The input does not list which relations count.

label: Has victim relation
summary: Whether the given character is the character's victim.
details: It checks the game's scripted relationship "victim" between the two characters. Vanilla uses it with saved scopes such as a victim, a hostage or a child.

label: Has ward relation
summary: Whether the given character is the character's ward.
details: It checks the scripted ward relationship between the two characters. Vanilla uses it with saved scopes such as a recipient or an imprisonment target, and `any_courtier = { has_relation_ward = scope:recipient }` to ask whether a courtier is the recipient's guardian. The game's relation definitions pair ward with guardian, so `has_relation_guardian` checks the same pair from the other side.

label: Has bad wedding fertility relation
summary: Whether the character has the bad wedding fertility relation with the given character.
details: It checks a scripted relationship by this name. Vanilla uses it once, with a `$CHARACTER$` placeholder, so what it means in play is not confirmed here.

summary: Whether the character has the good wedding fertility relation with the given character.

details: It checks the scripted relationship "wet nurse" between the two characters. Vanilla uses it six times, with saved scopes such as a wet nurse or an employee.

label: Has religion
summary: Whether the character has the given religion.
details: It compares the character's religion with a religion such as `religion:islam_religion`. Vanilla always writes the religion in that `religion:` form.

label: Has required heir governments
summary: Whether the holding type has required heir government types defined.
details: It runs on a holding type and takes `yes` or `no`. Vanilla uses it once, with `yes`.

label: Has revokable lease
summary: Whether the title is under a lease that can be revoked manually.
details: It runs on a title and takes `yes` or `no`. Vanilla uses it once, with `yes`.

label: Has revoke title reason
summary: Whether the character has the revoke title reason towards the given character.
details: The given character is the target of the reason. Vanilla uses it often, with saved scopes such as the recipient and with a `$VASSAL$` placeholder. The input does not say what makes up such a reason.

label: Has reward item
summary: Whether the player has a reward item.
details: An interface trigger: the game's documentation says it can only be used in specific places. The input shows no vanilla use.

label: Has royal court
summary: Whether the character has a royal court.
details: Takes `yes` or `no`. Vanilla uses it very often, mostly with `yes`.

label: Has ruined great building
summary: Whether the province has a ruined Great Building.
details: Takes `yes` or `no`. Vanilla uses it mostly with `no`.

label: Has ruler objective
summary: Whether the character has a ruler objective.
details: Takes `yes` or `no`. The input shows no vanilla use and does not explain what a ruler objective is.

label: Has saint character
summary: Whether the given character is a saint of the faith.
details: It runs on a faith and compares it with a character. Vanilla uses it with the saint in a province (`scope:province.saint_in_province`) or a named saved scope.

label: Has same court language
summary: Whether the character's court language is the same as the given character's.
details: Vanilla uses it mostly with saved scopes such as the recipient or the actor.

label: Has same court type
summary: Whether the character has the same court type as the given character.
details: The input shows no vanilla use and does not say which court types exist, so what is compared is only as the game's documentation states.

label: Has same culture
summary: Whether the character has the same culture as the given character.
details: Vanilla uses it with saved scopes such as the recipient or a vassal.

label: Has same culture ethos
summary: Whether the culture has the same ethos as the given culture.
details: It runs on a culture and compares with another culture. Vanilla mostly gives a character's culture such as `root.culture`.
